new ip but I can't open the web interface on it. also it keep rebooting.

Book with me <https://calendar.app.google/sqymqbycKJdV8y1j6>
Searched the web · Bitfortun BS-2 firmware v2 rebooting web interface
Searched the web · Harlo OS latest firmware version download harlolabs
Handed to the team · Needs JD: BS-2 reboot loop after a firmware update plus web UI unreachable, and

Hi Brendon,

Thanks for the extra detail, that changes the picture a bit, so let us sort the reboots before anything else. Do not install the overclock kit while the unit is restarting, it will only make the fault harder to read, and running the BS-2 above its rated 8.5 TH/s is overclocking, which sits outside the warranty.

First, the web interface. The B.2 shows its current IP on the onboard screen, so use the one on the screen rather than the old one, and type it with http:// in front (for example http://192.168.1.45), because browsers will otherwise try https and show nothing. Check your phone or laptop is on the same network, and on the same 2.4 GHz side if your router splits the bands. If the page loads for a second and dies, that is the miner rebooting under you, not the browser.

Second, power, which is the usual cause of a restart loop on these boards. Plug the Mean Well supply straight into a wall socket, no extension lead, no smart plug or surge strip in between, and press the XT60 connector fully home at the board end. If the unit runs fine for a minute and drops exactly when the hashrate ramps up, it is the supply sagging under load rather than the firmware.

Third, the update itself. If you applied v2 over the air, an over-the-air image that lands on top of old settings can leave the unit in a boot loop. The clean fix is a full install over USB from the flasher at https://harlolabs.com/ in Chrome or Edge: pick the device profile, connect the USB data cable, erase and install, then power it back up. Be aware the factory image wipes saved settings, so you will re-enter your Wi-Fi and pool details afterwards.

So JD can go straight at it if those do not settle it, could you send me three things: the exact firmware version and name the unit shows (whether it is Bitfortun v2 or Harlo OS with a version number), a short video of the screen from power on through to the moment it reboots, and a photo of the serial number label. I have passed everything so far to JD, our hardware lead, and he is picking this up today in this thread, along with the overclock kit steps. If you want it live instead of waiting, he is on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Searched the web · Harlo OS 0.2.100 release notes reboot

Hi Brendon,

That is useful, and it is good news in one way: a unit that comes back clean after a full power cycle is not a dead board. A watchdog reset or a brownout behaves exactly like that, twice in two weeks included, so let us go after the cause rather than the symptom.

0.2.100 is a version 2 build of Harlo OS, which is still public beta. The most common reason a BS-2 gets twitchy after a jump from v1 to v2 is the old saved settings surviving an over the air update. The config area carries values the new build reads differently, which shows up as random resets and a new IP. The clean fix is a full factory install over USB rather than another OTA: open the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, pick the BS-2 profile, connect a USB data cable, erase and install, then power up and let the self test run. While you are on that page, check the current build number against 0.2.100 and take the newest one. The factory image wipes saved settings, so have your Wi-Fi and pool details to hand to type back in.

Two things to do alongside that. Plug the Mean Well supply straight into a wall socket with nothing in between, no smart plug, no surge strip, and press the XT60 fully home, since a connector that is nearly seated gives you exactly this once a week pattern. And in your router, give the miner a fixed address by DHCP reservation, or run it on Ethernet, which Harlo OS always prefers over Wi-Fi. That stops the IP wandering, so when it does reboot you can still reach the dashboard.

Hold off on the overclock kit until it has run a week without a reset, and keep it at the rated 8.5 TH/s, since anything above that is overclocking and sits outside the warranty. If it drops again, the single most useful thing is a photo of the onboard screen just before or just after, with ASIC temp, VR temp and power visible, plus whether the water loop was still moving. Send that over and I will put it in front of JD.

JD has this thread today along with the overclock kit steps, and if you want it live he is on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Searched the web · heliumdeploy Overclocking kit power supply heatsinks thermal

Hi Brendon,

Good, here is the whole picture. The O. kit is a Mean Well LRS-350-12 power supply (12V, 29A), a thermal paste syringe, nine small aluminium heatsinks and two alcohol pads. Nothing in it is specific to the BS-2, which is why no printed steps went in the box.

Before anything else, one piece of advice given what we have been chasing this week. Your BS-2 has reset twice in two weeks, so do the clean factory install of Harlo OS first and let it run at stock for a few days. If you change the power supply, the clocks and the cooling all at once and it resets again, nobody can tell which change did it.

On the power supply. The B.2 draws around 150W at stock, so the 350W Mean Well is pure headroom, and it is also the part most likely to stop the resets if a sagging supply is behind them. Two things matter. Check the 115/230V selector switch on the LRS-350 and set it to match your mains before it ever sees power, because the wrong position will destroy it. And the LRS-350 is an open frame unit with bare screw terminals, so the mains side needs a properly made off lead with the terminal cover fitted. Please do not improvise that from a cut cable. If you are not set up to terminate mains cable safely, leave the stock supply on and just do the heatsinks, you lose nothing at stock clocks. On the DC side the existing XT60 lead goes to V+ and V-, polarity checked twice, with the unit unplugged while you work.

On the heatsinks. Unplug the miner and give it fifteen minutes to cool. On the BS-2 the voltage regulators sit on the back of the board in the fan path, and that is exactly where those nine heatsinks earn their keep, along with the power stages and the controller. Wipe each target with an alcohol pad and let it dry fully. Check whether your heatsinks have adhesive tape on the base: if they do, press and hold for thirty seconds each. If they are bare metal, thermal paste alone will not hold one on a vertical surface, so stop there and let JD tell you which adhesive he uses rather than gluing something permanently to the board. Keep them clear of the water block, the pump lead and the fan blades, and do not stack anything on the cold plate over the ASICs.

On actually clocking it up, once it has run clean for a few days. In Harlo OS raise frequency in small steps, around 25 MHz at a time, leave core voltage alone until frequency stops scaling, and give each step twenty minutes while you watch VR temperature, ASIC temperature and your pool's accepted shares. If rejects climb or the unit resets, you have found the ceiling, drop back one step. The stock values are always one click away in the interface. Worth saying plainly: running above the rated 8.5 TH/s is overclocking, and an overclocked unit is outside the warranty, so the kit is best thought of as cooling and power headroom first and extra hashrate second.

If you send me a photo of the back of the board and of the heatsink bases, I will have JD confirm placement before you stick anything down. He is in this thread, and he is quickest on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf if you mention @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
